drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Counsel, attached is our initial mark-up to put economic terms and standard executive protections into the draft. We have proposed a market package for a COO role of this scope, including a defined base salary, target bonus, equity grant, and a severance construct tied to termination without cause or resignation for good reason. We also narrowed the non-compete to make it more enforceable and proportionate while preserving legitimate business protections. Please let us know if Bellweather has any comments.

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. During the Term, the Executive shall receive: (a) an annual base salary of USD 1,250,000, payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices; (b) eligibility for an annual performance bonus with a target amount equal to 150% of annual base salary, subject to achievement of performance criteria established by the Board in good faith; (c) a one-time signing bonus of USD 2,000,000, payable within thirty (30) days after the Effective Date and subject to repayment on a pro rata basis if the Executive resigns without Good Reason or is terminated for Cause within twelve (12) months after the Effective Date; (d) an equity award with an aggregate grant-date value of USD 22,000,000, vesting 25% on the first anniversary of the Effective Date and monthly thereafter over the following thirty-six (36) months, subject to the terms of the applicable equity plan and award agreement; and (e) participation in employee benefit plans and executive perquisites made available to similarly situated senior executives.
edits.name: Compensation package

edits.text: 3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause or the Executive resigns for Good Reason, then, subject to the Executive’s execution and non-revocation of a customary release of claims, the Executive shall receive: (a) a cash severance payment equal to USD 7,000,000, payable in substantially equal installments over twelve (12) months; (b) any earned but unpaid annual bonus for any completed fiscal year; (c) a pro-rated target annual bonus for the fiscal year of termination; (d) twelve (12) months of Company-paid COBRA or equivalent health coverage continuation; and (e) accelerated vesting of the portion of the Executive’s then-outstanding equity awards that would have vested during the twelve (12) months following the termination date. For purposes of this Agreement, “Cause” and “Good Reason” shall be defined in a manner customary for public-company senior executive employment agreements.
edits.name: Severance

edits.text: 4. RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS. For twelve (12) months after the Executive’s separation from employment, the Executive shall not, within any jurisdiction in which the Company has material operations or demonstrable planned operations as of the separation date, directly provide services in a role substantially similar to the Executive’s role for the Company to a business that is materially competitive with the Company’s core products or services. This covenant shall not prohibit passive ownership of less than two percent (2%) of the outstanding securities of a publicly traded company, service to a non-competitive division or affiliate, or employment where the Executive’s duties do not involve the Company’s confidential information or competitive strategy. The Executive shall also comply with customary confidentiality, non-solicitation of employees and customers, and invention assignment obligations, each to be set forth in reasonable form.
edits.name: Non-compete narrowed

The revised package narrows the gap: lower base, target bonus, signing bonus, and equity; severance converted from a fixed $7M ask to 12 months’ base plus target bonus, COBRA, earned amounts, and limited equity acceleration. I also accepted the need for fully drafted definitions and covenants, but limited the non-compete to a role/product/geography nexus and added enforceability savings language.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Counsel,

Thank you. We have taken Vireo’s feedback seriously and have made substantial movement on economics and severance, while adding the requested defined terms and fully drafted restrictive covenant provisions. The revised draft reflects a balanced executive package: $1,000,000 base, 125% target bonus, a reduced $1,000,000 signing bonus with pro rata clawback, and a $15,000,000 equity grant on the standard four-year schedule.

On severance, we have moved away from the fixed cash severance structure and revised to 12 months of base salary plus target bonus, earned/unpaid amounts, 12 months’ COBRA, and 6 months of equity vesting acceleration, conditioned on a release and covenant compliance. We also drafted Cause and Good Reason with notice-and-cure mechanics, and included confidentiality, IP assignment, 12-month employee/customer non-solicits, and a tailored 12-month non-compete tied to the Company’s competitive business, the Executive’s role, and applicable law.

We think this should put the parties within closing range. Please let us know if Vireo can accept these revisions or has any final drafting comments.

edits.text: PARTIES. This Executive Employment Agreement is between Vireo Systems Inc., a Delaware corporation (the “Company”), and the Executive. The “Effective Date” shall be the date on which the Executive commences employment with the Company. The “Board” means the Company’s Board of Directors or a duly authorized committee thereof. The “Term” shall commence on the Effective Date and continue until terminated by either party in accordance with this Agreement.
edits.name: Parties and Defined Terms

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. During the Term, the Executive shall receive: (a) an annual base salary of USD 1,000,000, payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices and subject to annual review for increase by the Board; (b) eligibility for an annual performance bonus with a target amount equal to 125% of annual base salary, subject to achievement of performance criteria established by the Board in good faith, with any earned bonus payable at the same time annual bonuses are paid to similarly situated senior executives; (c) a one-time signing bonus of USD 1,000,000, payable within thirty (30) days after the Effective Date and subject to repayment on a pro rata basis if, within twelve (12) months after the Effective Date, the Executive resigns without Good Reason or is terminated for Cause; (d) an equity award with an aggregate grant-date value of USD 15,000,000, vesting 25% on the first anniversary of the Effective Date and monthly thereafter over the following thirty-six (36) months, subject to the terms of the Company’s equity incentive plan and the applicable award agreement; and (e) participation in employee benefit plans and executive perquisites made available to similarly situated senior executives.
edits.name: Compensation

edits.text: 3. SEVERANCE; CAUSE; GOOD REASON. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause or the Executive resigns for Good Reason, then, subject to the Executive’s execution and non-revocation of a customary release of claims and continued compliance with the restrictive covenants in this Agreement, the Executive shall receive: (a) continued payment of annual base salary for twelve (12) months following the termination date, payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices; (b) a cash amount equal to the Executive’s target annual bonus for the year of termination, payable in substantially equal installments over twelve (12) months; (c) any earned but unpaid annual bonus for any completed fiscal year; (d) any accrued but unpaid base salary, reimbursable business expenses, and vested employee benefits through the termination date; (e) twelve (12) months of Company-paid COBRA or equivalent health coverage continuation, subject to the Executive’s timely election and continued eligibility; and (f) accelerated vesting of the portion of the Executive’s then-outstanding time-based equity awards that would have vested during the six (6) months following the termination date. “Cause” means: (i) the Executive’s conviction of, or plea of guilty or nolo contendere to, a felony or crime involving fraud, dishonesty, or moral turpitude; (ii) willful misconduct or gross negligence in the performance of material duties that causes material harm to the Company; (iii) material breach of this Agreement or any written Company policy applicable to senior executives; (iv) fraud, embezzlement, or material misappropriation involving the Company; or (v) willful and continued failure to perform the Executive’s material duties after written notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure, if curable, of not less than thirty (30) days. “Good Reason” means, without the Executive’s written consent: (A) a material diminution in base salary or target bonus opportunity, other than an across-the-board reduction applicable to similarly situated senior executives; (B) a material diminution in authority, duties, or responsibilities; (C) a requirement that the Executive relocate the Executive’s principal place of employment by more than fifty (50) miles; or (D) a material breach by the Company of this Agreement; provided that the Executive gives written notice within ninety (90) days after the initial occurrence of the condition, the Company fails to cure within thirty (30) days after receipt of notice, and the Executive resigns within thirty (30) days after the cure period expires.
edits.name: Severance and Definitions

edits.text: 4. RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS. The Executive acknowledges that, in the course of employment, the Executive will receive and develop confidential information and goodwill of the Company. The Executive shall not, during or after employment, use or disclose any non-public confidential or proprietary information of the Company except as required in the good-faith performance of duties for the Company or as required by law. All inventions, works of authorship, developments, improvements, trade secrets, processes, know-how, data, software, designs, and other intellectual property conceived, developed, authored, or reduced to practice by the Executive, alone or with others, during employment and relating to the Company’s business, anticipated business, products, services, research, or development shall be the sole property of the Company, and the Executive hereby assigns all right, title, and interest therein to the Company. For twelve (12) months after the Executive’s separation from employment, the Executive shall not, directly or indirectly: (a) solicit for employment or hire any employee or individual service provider of the Company with whom the Executive had material business contact during the final twelve (12) months of employment, other than through general solicitations not targeted at such persons; (b) solicit any customer, prospective customer, vendor, supplier, or strategic partner with whom the Executive had material business contact or about whom the Executive received material confidential information during the final twelve (12) months of employment, for the purpose of providing products or services competitive with the Company’s business; or (c) within any jurisdiction in which the Company has material operations or demonstrable planned operations as of the separation date, provide services in a role substantially similar to the Executive’s role for the Company to any business that is materially competitive with the Company’s core products or services with respect to which the Executive had material responsibility or material confidential information during the final twelve (12) months of employment. The foregoing shall not prohibit passive ownership of less than two percent (2%) of the outstanding securities of a publicly traded company, service to a non-competitive division or affiliate, or employment where the Executive’s duties do not involve the Company’s confidential information, customers, strategic plans, or competitive products or services. Each covenant shall apply only to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, and any court of competent jurisdiction may reform an overbroad covenant to the minimum extent necessary to render it enforceable.
edits.name: Restrictive Covenants
